entities.summary: Pengiran Anak Mohamed Alam was a civil servant and noble magistrate who held the position of Pengiran Pemancha in Brunei. Serving from 1950 until 1982, this title marked him as the third most senior rank within the wazir class of state officials. He served as Brunei's first chief of Adat Istiadat Negara from 1954 to 1981 before assuming the role of the fourth speaker of the Legislative Council of Brunei (LegCo) from 1971 to 1974. Notably, he was the father of Queen Saleha, the raja isteri to Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, and the maternal grandfather of Al-Muhtadee Billah, the Crown Prince of Brunei.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As Pengiran Pemancha and fourth speaker of the Legislative Council of Brunei, he played a crucial role in shaping the country's governance and Adat Istiadat Negara. His tenure spanned over three decades, influencing the development of modern Brunei.
